nodes.summary: Every word-hyperbolic group is finitely generated.
nodes.title: Word-hyperbolic groups are finitely generated

nodes.summary: The word metric of the free group $F(\iota)$ with respect to its free basis is $0$-hyperbolic, for every set $\iota$ (for $\iota$ empty the group is trivial). Gromov notes that simplicial trees are $0$-hyperbolic, the Gromov product of two points being the distance from the base point to the segment joining them; the Cayley graph of a free group on a free basis is a tree, and the word metric is its path metric…
nodes.title: Free groups are `0`-hyperbolic

nodes.summary: If `f : G → X` satisfies `d(f g, f h) = |g⁻¹ h|_P` for all `g h` and `X` is `δ`-hyperbolic, then `G` with the word metric of `P` is `δ`-hyperbolic.
nodes.title: Word metrics isometric to a hyperbolic space are hyperbolic

nodes.summary: If $G$ is word-hyperbolic, then for every finite generating family $P$ of $G$ the word metric of $P$ is $\delta$-hyperbolic for some $\delta$ (depending on $P$). Gromov deduces it from the linear isoperimetric inequality (Corollary 2.3.B) and its converse (Theorem 2.3.D). It would also follow from the quasi-isometry invariance of hyperbolicity for quasi-geodesic spaces (word metrics are quasi-geodesic, Gromov 1993,…
nodes.title: Hyperbolicity does not depend on the finite generating set

nodes.summary: Every word-hyperbolic group is finitely presented (Mathlib's `Group.IsFinitelyPresented`). Gromov derives it from Rips's theorem: for $d \ge 4\delta + 1$ the Rips complex $P_d(\Gamma)$ is contractible, and $\Gamma$ acts on it properly and cocompactly.
nodes.title: Hyperbolic groups are finitely presented

nodes.summary: For the generator `ofAdd 1`, the word metric of `Multiplicative ℤ` is `d(ofAdd m, ofAdd n) = |m - n|`, isometric to `ℤ ⊆ ℝ`, hence `0`-hyperbolic (Gromov, *Hyperbolic groups*, 1987, §1.2(a)).
nodes.title: The infinite cyclic group is word-hyperbolic

nodes.summary: A group $G$ is word-hyperbolic if there are a finite index set $\iota$ and a family $(s_i)_{i \in \iota}$ of elements generating $G$ such that $G$, equipped with the word metric $d(g, h) = |g^{-1} h|$ of this generating family, is $\delta$-hyperbolic for some real number $\delta$.
nodes.title: Word-hyperbolic groups

nodes.summary: Every finite group is word-hyperbolic: for a finite generating family the word metric is bounded, and a bounded metric space is hyperbolic (Gromov, *Hyperbolic groups*, 1987, §1.2(b)).
nodes.title: Finite groups are word-hyperbolic

nodes.summary: Every trivial group is word-hyperbolic: the empty family generates it, and its word metric is $0$-hyperbolic.
nodes.title: The trivial group is word-hyperbolic

nodes.summary: If $G$ is word-hyperbolic and $P$ is a generating family of $G$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, then there is an algorithm deciding whether a word in the generators and their inverses represents the identity of $G$ (`WordProblemSolvable P.lift`, the predicate shared with the Boone–Higman and Novikov entries).
nodes.title: Hyperbolic groups have solvable word problem
